name: Twelve Costumes
summary: Ambrose Quill has found the old troupe's program, scrambled, and wants every costume matched to its player before the parade turns it into a souvenir.

stages.journal: Quill, in the festival, has a torn program of Chuckles's old troupe with its six players and costumes crossed out and mixed. He swears the right matching is a verse waiting to happen.
stages.hint: Match the six players to their costumes: look around the booths, or ask the crowd.

stages.journal: The program is right at last, and Quill has a rhyme about every one.
Quill read out his verses. Only two of them scanned, and one of those by accident.
The parade began and Quill's program went into the bonfire with the rest of the paper. He wrote the rhyme anyway.
